newsitem.title: USA: Olympic Cascade to pay 5pct stock dividend.
newsitem.headline: Olympic Cascade to pay 5pct stock dividend.

text.p: Olympic Cascade Financial Corp, reporting lower net earnings for the quarter ended June 27, said Friday it would pay a five percent stock dividend on September 8 to stockholders of record on August 29.
The brokerage firm posted a $86,000 net on revenues of $11.1 million in the quarter ended June 27, compared with a $523,000 net on revenues of $9.8 million the year before.
Olympic said it took charges of $300,000 in the quarter to pay for buying three broker-dealers.
"These non-operating, non-recurring expenses represent an investment in a strong foundation upon which we can grow," said chief executive Steven Rothstein in a statement.
The company bought instutional investment banker L.H. Friend, Weinress, Frankson & Presson Inc in March; WestAmerica Investment Group in June; and Travis Capital Inc in July.
Olympic's chief financial officer Bob Daskal said in an interview the acquisitions caused the drop in net income.

"There were some other operating expenses relating to the acquisitions in addition to the $300,000 charge," Daskal said. He added the acquisitions would contribute to the company's revenues, but declined to project their effect on its bottom line.
Olympic is a holding company for National Securities Corp, which has 38 offices in 18 states.
Olympic's stock dropped 15/16 to 5-1/4 Friday morning.
